cryptohome: Fix error code on non-existing chall-resp mount Return CRYPTOHOME_ERROR_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND from MountEx requests of KEY_TYPE_CHALLENGE_RESPONSE when the home directory doesn't exist and the request doesn't have the |create| field. This is important, since Chrome, even when signing the user in for the first time on the device, sends the first MountEx *without* the |create| field. Chrome then repeats this request *with* the |create| field, but only if the first request returned the non-fatal CRYPTOHOME_ERROR_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND error. This CL simply aligns the cryptohomed's challenge-response mount behavior with the existing and correct password-based mount behavior. BUG=chromium:842791 TEST=tast run $IP hwsec.ChallengeResponseMount Change-Id: Iaacafc575a16b127171dad811548a57b27436748 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1678657 Tested-by: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ryo Hashimoto <hashimoto@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: bluetooth: Enable filter duplicates field for passive scan This sets the filter duplicates field in LE Set Scan Enabled command to enabled for passive scanning. By enabling the field, the advertisement reports from the same address would be sent to the host once per passive scan cycle. However, since the buffer to keep the seen address is limited (e.g. the size of buffer is 50 for Intel controllers), the host will still be interrupted by any advertisement report with new addresses beyond the size of the buffer. BUG=b:128319712 TEST=(1) Pair and connect Microsoft BluetoothMouse3600 LE mouse from Bluetooth setting page. (2) Start btmon and confirm the mouse is connected by moving the mouse and observe ATT data in btmon. (3) Turn off the mouse and wait for 30 seconds. btmon prints HCI traffic of passive scanning. And the filtering duplicates was applied to at least 50 addresses in Bluetooth-noisy environment. Change-Id: I3a7b460facc6a1198c1a6f49cf476499f4ec91ca Signed-off-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1682455 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org>

cryptohome: Refactor DoCheckKeyEx arguments Make Service::DoCheckKeyEx() receive the arguments via std::unique_ptr rather than via raw pointers. The raw pointers are only valid while the function is executing (due to the base::Owned semantics), which doesn't allow accessing them in posted tasks. This refactoring allows to extend the DoCheckKeyEx implementation in follow-up CLs to support asynchronous challenge-response vault keyset verification. CHROMIUM: adapter: Prevent cleaning up temporary devices during active scanning. bluetoothd is supposed to clean up temporary devices after 3 minutes of scanning absence, the logic was implemented using a timer that would be triggered 3 minutes after the last scanning stops. This could cause the following problem: 1. Chrome starts scanning. 2. Chrome stops scanning (timer starts counting to 3 minutes). 3. Nothing happens for 2 minutes 50 seconds. 4. Chrome starts scanning. 5. 10 seconds later, the timer created by step 2 triggers bluetoothd to clean up the scanning result (in the middle of Chrome scanning session). 6. Chrome stops scanning. In this change we cancel the timer if it exists when a new scanning starts. BUG=chromium:959306 TEST=manual tests via bluetoothctl with the following steps: 1. Turn scanning on 2. Turn scanning off after some devices have been discovered. 3. Count to 2 minutes 50 seconds. 4. Turn scanning on again. 5. Observe that the devices are not removed crossing the 3 minute mark. 6. Turn scanning off. 7. Wait for 3 minutes. 8. Observe the temp devices are deleted in the terminal. 9. The 'devices' command should return empty list. We were not sleeping after writing this out, so it's very possible that we would get the wrong consent state back from the metrics library. Adding a 2 second sleep after every time we change it should resolve that problem.
